sources.entry: MiniSim - MacOS menu bar app for launching iOS  and Android 🤖 emulators.

summary.one_liner: MiniSim is a small macOS menu bar app for launching iOS Simulator and Android emulators.
summary.what_it_does: MiniSim is a lightweight menu bar utility written in Swift and AppKit that lists and launches iOS and Android emulators from the macOS menu bar. For iOS simulators it can copy the device UDID and name and delete simulators. For Android emulators it can cold boot, run without audio, toggle a11y on the selected emulator, and copy the device name or ADB id. It can focus devices using the accessibility API, set default launch flags, and indicate which devices are running. The menu can be opened with a global shortcut (⌥ + ⇧ + e). The README says it fetches available devices through xcrun and the Android sdk/emulator tools.
use_cases: launch iOS simulators from the menu bar
copy simulator UDID or ADB id
how_to_run: Or download the app from the releases page
notable: Launches both iOS Simulator and Android emulators from one menu bar app
Global shortcut ⌥ + ⇧ + e to open the menu
Focus devices via the accessibility API
Optional Raycast extension works alongside it
caveats: Depends on a working Xcode and Android Studio setup; may not work without them
Requires macOS, since it is a menu bar app built with Swift and AppKit
README does not describe a license
